at_note: verified on real conversation-blobs.db data + product source
method: read-only scan of every agent's conversation-blobs.db; recompute sha256(data) and compare to the row id; check whether any single content maps to more than one id (a dedup violation)

sourceProof.CORRECTION_perGPT: Earlier this file claimed line 17 ENFORCES id==sha256(data) at write time. That is wrong. setBlob(id,data) (line 14) stores the CALLER-SUPPLIED id + bytes; it does not compute the id. The createHash('sha256')...!==id comparison on line 17 lives INSIDE clearStaleCheckpointRoots() and is used to SELECT stale checkpoint-root candidates (skip rows whose id is not its content sha), NOT to validate writes.
sourceProof.whatSchemaGuarantees: conversation-blob-store.ts:11 INSERT INTO blobs(id,data) ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE + PRIMARY KEY(id) guarantees ID UNIQUENESS (same id upserts to one row). It does NOT by itself guarantee content-addressing: the same bytes under two different ids would be two rows.
sourceProof.contentAddressingIsProducerContract: id == sha256(content) is a PRODUCER contract (the writer computes the content sha as the id), not a store-enforced invariant. The real-data scan below is EMPIRICAL evidence the producer does this in practice, not a proof the schema enforces it.
sourceProof.schema: blobs(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data BLOB NOT NULL) STRICT

liveData.mismatchExplanation: the 12 non-sha ids all begin with hex 73616e642d6c6976652d = 'sand-live-' — symbolic root/pointer entries (one per db), NOT content-addressed data blobs

result: PARTIAL (empirical dedup on stored data; full attachment HTTP path not run)
scope_perGPT: This is real-DATA evidence that the STORED conversation blobs are content-addressed and dedup'd in practice (the producer computes id=sha256(content)). It is NOT: (a) a proof the schema enforces content-addressing (it does not — see sourceProof CORRECTION), nor (b) the full L38 attachment acceptance path. Plan L38 (line 315) additionally requires: same name + DIFFERENT bytes attached to different agents, upload response-loss + retry, chunked fetch, wrong path rejection, and source-vs-fetch SHA match over the real attachment API with per-agent target isolation. Those remain OPEN; this scan is supporting evidence only.
notes: 20,427/20,439 stored ids == sha256(data) (12 exceptions are symbolic sand-live-* root pointers); 20,407 distinct contents -> 0 mapped to >1 id. Schema (PRIMARY KEY + upsert) guarantees id uniqueness; content-addressing is a producer contract that the data shows is honored in practice.
